The `git reflog` command provides a history of HEAD movements, and by examining this history, we can identify the commit that was cherry-picked and later reset. The commit we are interested in is referenced at `HEAD@{1}`, which is the state immediately before the reset operation. Using `git reset --hard HEAD@{1}` allows us to revert the repository to the state right after the cherry-pick, effectively recovering the commit.

```bash
git reset --hard HEAD@{1}
```

This command resets the current branch to the state at `HEAD@{1}`, which is the commit that was cherry-picked and subsequently reset. This approach directly utilizes the reflog to pinpoint and restore the desired commit, ensuring that the repository is returned to the state right after the cherry-pick operation.
